headline: High: Semantic Kernel can write/read shared files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools, while Pathway is a document-processing component with no isolation, creating default risks of leakage, conflict, and unverified cascading actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no shared channel or input surface documented, so it is not itself an injection source. Semantic Kernel can call MCP/OpenAPI tools and process application-defined files, so if Pathway outputs are routed into SK without provenance checks, prompt-like content in documents can steer tool use. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are fed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Semantic Kernel treats document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool calls.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt.
Strip or escape tool-like directives from Pathway outputs.
Require human review before any tool call triggered by document text.
Log and flag any prompt containing file-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing component with filesystem access disabled, but Semantic Kernel can read and write application-defined files and send context to external model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools. If both operate on the same workspace, Pathway content can flow into SK and then out to third parties. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file set, Pathway documents can be exposed to Semantic Kernel.
IF Semantic Kernel forwards file contents to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP/OpenAPI tools, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable external model/tool calls for sensitive documents.
Redact secrets before Semantic Kernel ingestion.
Restrict SK file access to a narrow allowlist.
Review outbound destinations for each plugin.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files or modify git state, while Semantic Kernel can write the filesystem and uses application-defined files. That reduces direct write-write conflict, but if both are pointed at the same directory, SK can overwrite or race with Pathway-produced artifacts. Because the orchestrator locking model is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, Semantic Kernel can overwrite Pathway outputs.
IF the orchestrator provides no locking, concurrent writes can corrupt shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Enable file locks around shared writes.
Make Pathway outputs read-only to Semantic Kernel.
Serialize write phases in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing system, so its outputs are likely to be consumed downstream. Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs and call external APIs. If SK treats Pathway-produced text or extracted facts as authoritative, errors can cascade into irreversible external actions. The interaction is inferred from roles, but the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Pathway output as authoritative input, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF SK plugins send emails, tickets, or API mutations based on Pathway extraction, errors become externally visible.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking plugin.
Require confidence thresholds for extracted facts.
Keep Pathway outputs advisory only.
Add rollback or approval gates for external actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send data to external providers, while Pathway is a document-processing component with no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated documents flow from Pathway into SK, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents, SK's outbound calls may create residency or retention issues.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or retention policy alignment, compliance gaps can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before SK ingestion.
Block regulated data from outbound model calls.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document residency for each plugin/provider.
Review DPA and vendor terms before deployment.
